labels.text: How can I help you today?

S20.01.note: The shape of the answer is chosen by the model, so the test depends on what it writes.
steps: Sign in and open Chat.
Click the box that shows "How can I help you today?", type "Write two short paragraphs about the sea", and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the two paragraphs are separate blocks with a gap between them.
S20.01.where: Chat > type "Write two short paragraphs about the sea" in the box that shows "How can I help you today?" > send

S20.02.note: Heading styles are in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx; the model chooses whether to write headings.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Answer with a title using # and a sub-heading using ##" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the title and sub-heading appear larger and bolder, with no # marks shown.
S20.02.where: Chat > type "Answer with a heading and a smaller sub-heading" in the chat box > send

S20.03.note: Depends on the model writing the markers in its reply.
steps: Open Chat.
Type the sentence with **bold**, *italic* and ~~strikethrough~~ and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: bold text is heavier, italic is slanted, and the struck text has a line through it.
S20.03.where: Chat > type "Write one sentence with **bold**, *italic* and ~~strikethrough~~ words" in the chat box > send

S20.04.note: Start-number behaviour depends on the model writing the list with that start.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "List 3 tips as a numbered list starting at 3" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the list shows numbers 3, 4, 5 with indentation.
S20.04.where: Chat > type "List 3 tips as a numbered list starting at 3" in the chat box > send

steps: Open Chat.
Type "List 3 fruits using dash bullets" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: each item has a bullet marker and is indented.
S20.05.where: Chat > type "List 3 fruits using dash bullets" in the chat box > send

S20.06.note: The code audit could not find the quoted line any more, but the list renderers in MarkdownContent.tsx still exist.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Give a list with one sub-list nested under an item" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the sub-list sits under its parent item with deeper indentation.
S20.06.where: Chat > type "Give a list with one sub-list nested under an item" in the chat box > send

S20.07.note: Not checked whether a checkbox can be clicked to change it; Expected does not require that.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Make a checklist with one unchecked and one checked item" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the items show empty and ticked checkboxes that match their state.
S20.07.where: Chat > type "Make a checklist with - [ ] and - [x] items" in the chat box > send

steps: Open Chat.
Type "Quote a short line of a poem using > at the start" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the quoted line sits in an indented block that looks different from normal text.
S20.08.where: Chat > type "Quote a short line of a poem using >" in the chat box > send

S20.09.note: Rendering is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx; the model decides whether to write one.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Write one line, then a line of three dashes, then one more line" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: a thin horizontal divider appears between the two lines.
S20.09.where: Chat > type "Write one line, then a line of three dashes, then one more line" in the chat box > send

S20.10.note: The quoted code line moved; the inline code renderer is still in MarkdownContent.tsx.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Use the word `inline code` in one sentence" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the code words appear in a monospace style that differs from the sentence text.
S20.10.where: Chat > type "Use the word `inline code` in one sentence" in the chat box > send

S20.11.note: The quoted code line moved; the block renderer is in MarkdownContent.tsx and CodeBlock.tsx.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Show a short Python function in a fenced code block with indentation" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the code is in a monospace block with its indentation kept and a "Copy" button at the top right.
S20.11.where: Chat > type "Show a short Python function in a code block" in the chat box > send

S20.12.note: Click opens an external link through shell.openExternal in apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts.
steps: Open Chat.
Type the request for a link and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: "Sea" appears as blue underlined text with a small arrow icon.
Click it and see that it opens outside the chat, in a new window or tab.
S20.12.where: Chat > type "Give me a link to the Wikipedia page on the sea, with the link text 'Sea'" in the chat box > send

S20.13.note: Link handling is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx and remarkPlugins.ts.
steps: Open Chat.
Type "Include the full web address https://example.com in your reply" and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the bare web address appears as a link that can be clicked.
S20.13.where: Chat > type "Include the full web address https://example.com in your reply" in the chat box > send

S20.14.note: Footnote handling is in MarkdownContent.tsx (footnote link code); whether the marker is styled as superscript was not confirmed. Depends on the model writing a footnote.
steps: Open Chat.
Type the footnote request and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the reference shows as a small raised marker.
Click the marker and check that it jumps to the matching footnote at the bottom.
S20.14.where: Chat > type "Answer with one footnote reference and its footnote at the end" in the chat box > send

steps: Open Chat.
Type the table request and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the table has a header row, a grid of cells and aligned columns.
Hover over the table to see its buttons.
S20.15.where: Chat > type "Make a table comparing 3 fruits by price and colour" in the chat box > send

S20.16.needs: a wide table in an answer
S20.16.note: Rule is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx (markdownTableWrapClass comment). Code audit did not confirm the exact scroll behaviour.
steps: Ask in Chat for a table with 10 or more columns and send.
Make the app window narrow by dragging its edge.
Compare: the table scrolls sideways inside its own area and the rest of the page does not scroll sideways or get cut off.
S20.16.where: Inside a table in an answer, when the window is narrow. Table code uses a scroll region inside the table.

S20.18.note: Only CSV was found in code; no XLSX download control was found. Buttons are hidden until hover or focus, except on touch screens.
steps: Ask in Chat for a table and send.
Move the mouse over the table so its buttons show.
Click "Download as CSV".
Compare: a CSV file with the table contents is saved to the computer.
S20.18.where: Chat > answer with a table > hover over the table > Download as CSV

S20.19.note: Math handling is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/preprocessMath.ts and MarkdownContent.tsx.
steps: Open Chat.
Type the request with the inline formula in $...$ and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the formula appears typeset as maths inside the sentence, not as raw $ signs.
S20.19.where: Chat > type "Write the formula $E=mc^2$ inside a sentence" in the chat box > send

S20.20.note: Also accepts \[...\] per the code; not tested here.
steps: Open Chat.
Type the request with the display formula in $$...$$ and send.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare: the formula appears centred on its own line as typeset maths.
S20.20.where: Chat > type "Show the formula $$E=mc^2$$ on its own line" in the chat box > send

S20.21.note: Code is in packages/platform/utils/src/markdownSource.ts and preprocessMath.ts; whether the model keeps the backslashes is not controlled by the app.
steps: Send in Chat: "Repeat this exactly: 5 \$ 3 and \*not italic\*".
Wait for the reply.
Compare: the characters show without the backslashes and the text is not turned into italic.
S20.21.where: In an answer that contains backslash-escaped characters such as \* or \$.

S20.22.note: Streaming renderer is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx; the reply is only partial for a short time.
steps: Send in Chat a request for a long answer with a heading and a list, such as "Write a 300-word guide with headings and bullet points".
Watch the answer while it is still arriving.
Compare: headings and bullets appear as formatted text as they come in, not as # or - symbols.
S20.22.where: Shown while a reply is still arriving in the chat, in the answer bubble.

S20.23.note: Hard to time by hand; the completion code is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/completeInlineTokens.ts.
steps: Send in Chat "Write a long Python script in one code block".
Watch the answer while it is still arriving, before the code block is closed.
Compare: the unfinished code shows inside a code block box, not as plain text, until the block closes.
S20.23.where: Shown in an answer bubble while a reply with a code block is still arriving.

S20.24.note: Sanitizing is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx and the message code in MessageBubble.tsx.
steps: Send in Chat: "Write this exact text: and bold html".
Wait for the reply.
Compare: no pop-up or script runs; the tags show as inert text or are removed, and nothing executes.
S20.24.where: In an answer, where model-written HTML or script tags appear as text.

S20.25.note: Unsafe schemes such as javascript: are stripped to plain text by the code; testing them needs a prompt that writes them. External opening is handled in apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts.
steps: Get an answer with a web link in Chat.
Hover the link and read its address in the status bar at the bottom of the window.
Click the link.
Compare: it opens outside the app in the browser, and the app stays on the chat.
S20.25.where: Chat > click a link in an answer, such as the one from "Give me a link to the Wikipedia page on the sea"

S20.26.note: The quoted code moved; no blocker on selection was found in MarkdownContent.tsx or CodeBlock.tsx. Not checked whether the code block box stops a drag.
steps: Get an answer with a paragraph, a list and a code block in Chat.
Press the mouse button at the start of the first paragraph.
Drag down through the list and the code block.
Compare: the whole run of text across all blocks is highlighted in one selection.
Press Command+C and paste into a text field to check the copied text.
S20.26.where: Chat > in one answer, drag the mouse from the first paragraph down through a list and a code block

S20.27.needs: a conversation with answers that contain the searched word
S20.27.note: Both Cmd+F handlers exist; in the Electron desktop the menu accelerator (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts) likely wins, so the "Find in page" bar is probably what opens, not the in-conversation bar. Not verified by running the app.
steps: Open a conversation that has several assistant answers containing a common word.
Press Cmd+F (or choose Edit > Find > Find… in the desktop app).
Type the word in the "Search messages..." box (or the "Find in page" box).
Look for the matching words highlighted in the answers and the count such as "1 of 3 matches"; press Return to jump to the next match and Shift+Return for the previous one.
S20.27.where: Open a conversation with answers > press Cmd+F > the "Search messages..." bar opens at the top of the messages. On the desktop app, Edit > Find > Find… opens the "Find in page" bar instead (the desktop find bar also highlights text in answers).

S20.28.needs: a conversation with formatted answers (headings, lists, a table, code, math)
S20.28.note: The Export dialog's PDF path goes through apps/web/features/chat/services/document-export-service.ts; Print uses the browser print dialog (apps/web/features/chat/lib/print-conversation.ts). Artifact downloads (Download as PDF / Word) are a separate menu and were not used here. Not verified by running the app.
steps: Open a conversation that has headings, a list, a table and a code block in an answer.
Click the "Conversation options" button and choose Print; in the print dialog check the preview keeps headings, lists, tables and code.
Or click "Conversation options" and choose Export…, then pick PDF or Word Document under "Export Format" and download the file.
Open the saved file and compare headings, lists, tables, code and math with the on-screen answer.
S20.28.where: Open a conversation > click the "Conversation options" button > Print (prints the whole transcript, expanded). Or "Conversation options" > Export… > Export Chat History > choose PDF or Word Document > Export.

S20.29.needs: none (a keyboard that can type Arabic or Hebrew helps)
S20.29.note: Direction comes from the browser's dir="auto" on the message text, not from a visible setting. Per-paragraph direction was not found in MarkdownContent.tsx; a mixed-language answer may take its direction from the whole message. Not verified by running the app.
steps: Type a sentence in Arabic or Hebrew in the message box and send it.
Look at the sent bubble: the text should start on the right and read right to left.
Ask for a reply in Arabic or Hebrew and check the assistant bubble is also right-aligned, with punctuation at the correct end of the line.
S20.29.where: No control of its own; the direction is set per message by the browser (dir="auto" on the message text). Effect is seen in the chat bubble after sending right-to-left text.

labels.text: This diagram could not be drawn

S20.30.needs: none; a failed diagram depends on the assistant's output and cannot be forced from the UI
S20.30.note: Unknown card kinds fall back to a headline and text box in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/InteractiveCardBlock.tsx (no visible control; happens only when the server sends an unrecognised card). The unknown-language code block fallback was not located. Not verified by running the app.
steps: Start a new chat and ask the assistant for a flowchart as a Mermaid diagram.
If the drawing fails, look for the message "This diagram could not be drawn" with a reason line.
Check that the source text is still shown below the message with a copy control, and that the rest of the answer is still visible.
Optionally ask for an unknown code language block and check it still shows as readable text.
S20.30.where: New chat > ask the assistant for a Mermaid diagram (a ```mermaid block). If the diagram fails to draw, the message shows "This diagram could not be drawn" with the source kept below.
